info.title: Latexy-Backend
info.description: LaTeX resume compilation and optimization service

post.description: Submit a new job to the async queue.

Compile LaTeX with a watermark overlay.

The resulting PDF is a one-off temporary file — it is NOT stored as
the canonical PDF for the resume and does NOT trigger an auto-save
checkpoint.  Download via GET /download/{job_id} once the job
completes.

Metered exactly like /jobs/submit's latex_compilation: authenticated callers
spend a ``compilations`` unit, anonymous callers must pass the device trial.
It runs the same pdflatex, so leaving it unmetered would make the whole
compile allowance one endpoint away from being bypassed.

Fork a resume once per job description and submit a combined optimize+compile
job for each fork.  Returns immediately; clients poll /jobs/batch/{batch_id}.

get.description: Return per-job status for a batch and an aggregated batch-level status.
Get current job state snapshot (for REST polling fallback).
Fetch the final job result (available after job.completed event).

Replay all Redis Stream events for a job (HTTP fallback for WebSocket reconnects).

Returns the ordered list of events stored in latexy:stream:{job_id}.
Clients that missed events while disconnected can catch up by hitting this
endpoint and then re-subscribing to the WebSocket.

Query param:
  from_id — Stream entry ID to start from (default "0" = beginning).
            Pass the last seen stream_id to get only new events.

delete.description:
Request cancellation of a running job.

Sets latexy:job:{job_id}:cancel flag in Redis.  Celery workers poll
is_cancelled() between stages and stop gracefully.

get.description:
List recent jobs for the authenticated user (reads from user ZSET).

Get job system health: Redis status plus real queue depths and workers.

The ``status`` field is driven solely by Redis so deployment probes stay
stable. ``queue_depths`` and ``worker_count`` are aggregate best-effort
enrichments; a snapshot-table outage or an empty broker never flips the
probe unhealthy, and no job payloads or Redis credentials are ever exposed.

Browsers cannot attach an Authorization header to a WebSocket handshake.
Exchanging the normal session over authenticated HTTP prevents the reusable
seven-day Better Auth token from appearing in WebSocket URLs and access logs.

get.description:
Redirect to the PNG thumbnail on object storage (R2).

Serving via a presigned redirect lets the browser fetch straight from the
storage/CDN edge instead of proxying every image through the backend
(backend->R2->backend->client). Across a 147-template grid that removes a
round-trip per thumbnail. Falls back to streaming if presigning is
unavailable so a misconfigured environment still works.

head.description: Check if a PDF exists in MinIO (lightweight — no body download).

get.description:
Redirect to the pre-compiled PDF on object storage (R2).

Same rationale as the thumbnail: the browser fetches from the storage/CDN
edge instead of streaming through the backend, which also renders the
preview <iframe> faster. R2 serves the object without X-Frame-Options, so
it embeds cleanly. Falls back to streaming if presigning is unavailable.
